solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Do avoid that hot sauce

blocks.note: to cut someone is to avoid or ignore them
the definite article, as in 'that one' = 'the one'

explanation.surface: Advice to someone about to eat: steer clear of the fiery sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a kitchen instruction, 'Do' looks like the start of a command; it is the definition, meaning 'be good enough', as in 'that will do'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut the mustard is to be good enough, which is what something does when it will do.

clue.text: French philosopher quietly barred from college grounds

blocks.note: the grounds of a college or university
p = piano, quietly in music; it is removed

explanation.surface: A French thinker being kept off a university site.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Camus, the writer of The Outsider, is the philosopher; the surface's banning order is literally what happens to the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French philosopher and novelist associated with absurdism.

clue.text: Puzzling pieces of square brown mass

blocks.note: a gram is a unit of mass

explanation.surface: Some baffling bits of a square that is brown and heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs longer than it looks: 'Puzzling pieces of square' is the whole of it, since a tangram is a square cut into seven pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangram is a Chinese puzzle of seven pieces cut from a square and rearranged into shapes.

clue.text: Giddy bachelor showered, taking maiden’s place in seraglio

blocks.note: m = maiden, a cricket over with no runs; it is swapped out
b = bachelor; it takes M's place, making HAREB

explanation.surface: A dizzy single man takes a shower and then stands in for a woman in a harem.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored, hence M; the one-letter swap happens before the weather word is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Harebrained means rash or flighty, much like giddy in its sense of frivolous.

clue.text: Reflecting less concern

blocks.note: more matt, the comparative of matt, a surface that shines less
a concern here is a business or affair, the noun

explanation.surface: Someone thinking about things less and so caring less.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading MATTER as matt + -er: a matt finish reflects less light than a glossy one. 'Reflecting' pretends to mean thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Two plain senses: the comparative of matt, a dull finish that throws back less light, and the noun for an affair, as in 'a matter for the police'.

clue.text: Arctic hunter broadcast cry of distress around north

indicators.note: Something placed around another encloses it.

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering
n = north, placed inside SOW to make SNOW
a yowl is a loud wail

explanation.surface: A radio message about a hunter in the far north sending a distress call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and 'cry of distress' together suggest an SOS on the radio; broadcast is the farmer's word, sowing seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowy owl is a large white owl that hunts on the Arctic tundra.

clue.text: One speed if short of power

indicators.note: To be short of something is to lack it.

explanation.surface: A single gear on a vehicle that is underpowered.
explanation.walkthrough: An ace is the one in a pack of cards, which is why 'One' can define it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ace is the card valued at one, and on dice the one-spot face.

clue.text: Peter out first on deck, totally calm abandoning ship

indicators.note: take the opening letter of 'deck'

explanation.surface: A becalmed sailing scene where Peter comes up on deck first and then leaves the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a sailor's name; with 'out' it is the verb meaning to fade away.
explanation.definitionFit: To peter out is to diminish gradually to nothing, which is what dwindling does.

clue.text: American blues fan daughter converted to Cream

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: An American blues lover whose daughter has come round to the rock band Cream.
explanation.walkthrough: In US politics blue is the Democrats' colour, so a blues fan is a Democrat supporter, not a music lover; Cream was a 1960s blues-rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue states vote Democratic, so an American who backs the blues is a Democrat.

clue.text: Live in effectively brand-new tower

indicators.note: One word goes in another, the plain sense of placing something inside.

blocks.note: in mint condition = as good as new
to be is to live: 'we are' = 'we live'

explanation.surface: Moving into a tower block that has only just been built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live in' reads as one phrase about residence; 'in' is really the container instruction, and 'effectively brand-new' is a single idea, as good as new.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower is the general word; a minaret is one particular kind, the slender tower beside a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Earlier group taken through Yosemite now back

indicators.note: a run of letters is lifted from across the words
the run reads right to left

blocks.note: yosEMITE NOw contains the letters, which are then read backwards

explanation.surface: An old party of hikers passing through Yosemite and now returning.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words, so the national park is only a letter carrier here.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means former, as in 'a one-time champion', i.e. earlier.

clue.text: Rose’s bed maybe quiet and springy

explanation.surface: A woman named Rose has a soft, bouncy, peaceful bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose looks like a person's name with a mattress; it is the flower, and her bed is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrubbery is an area planted with shrubs, which may be where roses grow.

clue.text: Valued bijou scratched in odd places, reproduction you hear

indicators.note: letters 1, 3, 5... are struck out, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A precious little trinket that has been scratched in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratched' deletes rather than marks, and 'odd places' says which letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio is recorded or transmitted sound, a reproduction that you listen to.

clue.text: Spooner’s bred ’ackneys etc for the military

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: farmed = bred; it hands its F over
hackneys and the like are horses, with the H dropped as the apostrophe shows; it takes the F

explanation.surface: Horses bred for use by the army, in a Cockney-flavoured spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ackneys matters: FARMED 'ORSES has only the F to swap, giving ARMED FORCES. A hackney is a breed of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces are a country's military services taken together.

clue.text: Gong with two sides, neither having echo

blocks.note: a side is a team; two of them
Echo is E in the radio alphabet; removed from each TEAM

explanation.surface: A gong that can be struck on both faces yet gives back no echo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two sides' sounds like the faces of the gong; it means two teams, each shedding its E.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the tam-tam is the orchestra's large flat bronze gong, named after its sound.

clue.text: Ill-judged time to show more of the real you?

blocks.clueFragment: to show more of the real you?
blocks.note: to act less, putting on less of a performance

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is a bad moment to reveal your true self.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'show more of the real you' is a playful way of saying ACT LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactless remark is ill-judged, lacking sensitivity.

clue.text: Curse, stuffing one’s weight in bikini?

indicators.note: Stuffing something fills its inside, so the curse word is filled with the other letters.

explanation.surface: Cursing at squeezing into a bikini.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark says a bikini is only an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: the bikini is a single instance of the whole category.

clue.text: Italian greeting chief heard order in Chinese

indicators.note: what we want is how the words sound

explanation.surface: A leading Italian giving a command in a Chinese language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as a command; it is a meal ordered in a Chinese restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a dish of fried noodles often ordered at a Chinese takeaway.

clue.text: Light speed and Mach one confused Native American

indicators.note: Something confused is jumbled and out of order, so these letters are rearranged.

blocks.note: c is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: Someone muddled by light speed versus the speed of sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light speed and Mach one' reads as physics; the first contributes just C, the second its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Comanche are a Native American people of the southern Great Plains.

clue.text: Drink from craft baby bottles

indicators.note: To bottle something is to hold it inside a container, so one word holds the other.

explanation.surface: Feeding a baby from hand-crafted bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' looks like a noun about feeding a baby; it is the verb, MINI bottling ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Instructed party returned small batch of shares

explanation.surface: A group of people who were given orders came back with a few shares.
explanation.walkthrough: TOLD DO read backwards is ODD LOT. On a stock exchange an odd lot is a holding smaller than the usual trading unit.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd lot is a quantity of shares less than the standard round lot.

clue.text: Gap between seats Romeo spread with girl’s clothing

indicators.note: ROMEO's letters are spread about
just the outside layer of 'girl'

explanation.surface: A lover sprawling across the aisle with his girlfriend's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo wants to be the R of the radio alphabet; here all five letters are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is the space in front of a seat, such as the gap to the next row.

clue.text: Commercial imperative the very thing academic is superior to

blocks.note: 'it' as in 'that's it', exactly what's wanted

explanation.surface: Business needs versus the ideal, which the scholar claims to stand above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' sounds snobbish; in a down clue it just means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is what every commercial business must make.

clue.text: Horribly bright — you are to wear hat

blocks.note: lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Being told to put on a hat that is garishly coloured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You are' becomes text-speak, and the surface's order to put on a hat is the literal instruction: the hat goes round the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means unpleasantly vivid in colour.

clue.text: Belligerent type of friendly against Germany

explanation.surface: An aggressive player in a friendly football match against Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friendly' reads as a noun, a non-competitive match; it is the adjective WARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A warmonger is someone eager for war, a belligerent person.

clue.text: Outside the church, troops brought round for the king

indicators.note: Bringing something round turns it to face the other way, so the letters are read backwards.

explanation.surface: Soldiers gathering outside a church for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like a container instruction; 'outside the church' means not ordained, the laity. OR, other ranks, is the army's term for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal means belonging to or fit for a king.

clue.text: Hollow stick, one where it’s icy?

definitions.text: Hollow stick, one where it’s icy?

indicators.note: the word is emptied, leaving only its outside

explanation.surface: Asking about a hollow stick used on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: read straight, it describes a light tubular stick used on snow and ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: ski poles are hollow metal sticks, one in each hand, used on icy slopes, so the whole clue reads as a straight description.

clue.text: Two blood types primarily form clot

indicators.note: just the first letter of form

explanation.surface: Two blood groups that start a clot forming.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is medical, where a clot is blood; in British slang a clot is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot is British slang for a clumsy fool, a plain synonym once the medical sense is set aside.

clue.text: Blue-collar employer snubbed brave politician

indicators.note: cut short, as a snub nose is short

blocks.note: to brave something is to face it
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A factory owner who cold-shoulders a courageous MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' reads as a social slight; here it docks the end of FACE. 'Brave' is the verb, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory employs manual, blue-collar workers.

clue.text: During shivery semifinal it’s almost zero

indicators.note: Something shivery trembles and shakes, and shaken letters fall into a new order.

blocks.note: in = during, as in 'in the war'

explanation.surface: A nervous semifinalist whose chances are next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition; IT belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinitesimal means vanishingly small, all but zero.
